The analyzer normalizes input text before tokenization. Curly quotes map to their ASCII equivalents, dashes and ellipses are preserved for sentence splitting, and the tokenizer keeps tokens matching the pattern of one or more lowercase letters followed by an optional apostrophe and one or more lowercase letters. This matches the upstream reference implementation exactly, including its handling of edge apostrophes, which are stripped.

Scores are computed from three rates. The word rate counts how many tokens per thousand appear in the overused-word list. The trigram rate counts trigram hits per thousand tokens. The contrast rate counts pattern matches per thousand characters. Each rate is normalized against a calibration range derived from the upstream leaderboard results, with a ten percent buffer on each side, then clamped to the interval from zero to one. The final score is a weighted sum: sixty percent words, twenty-five percent contrast patterns, fifteen percent trigrams, scaled to one hundred.

Empty input produces no score. The report carries a warning instead, because a score computed against a degenerate denominator would be misleading. Short input is scored but flagged. All findings are sorted deterministically: scored evidence first, then diagnostics, then null-score documents last.
